learning_objective: 🤝 Understand why sharing power is the secret to a peaceful and successful democracy, using the real-world stories of Belgium and Sri Lanka!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: सत्ता की साझेदारी (सरकार के विभिन्न अंगों या समूहों के बीच शक्तियों का बंटवारा)
बहुसंख्यकवाद (यह मान्यता कि बहुसंख्यक समुदाय को अपने मनमाने ढंग से देश पर शासन करना चाहिए)
जातीय (समान संस्कृति, भाषा या इतिहास पर आधारित सामाजिक विभाजन)
समायोजन (विवादों को टालने के लिए सभी समूहों को सरकार में उचित प्रतिनिधित्व देना)
युक्तिपरक (लाभ-हानि का सावधानीपूर्वक हिसाब लगाकर लिया गया फैसला)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In Sri Lanka, the Sinhala majority forced their dominance over the Tamil minority through the 1956 Act (making Sinhala the only official language). This denial of power-sharing led to alienation, conflict, and a devastating civil war.

Belgium faced a similar ethnic tension between Dutch and French speakers. Instead of fighting, they amended their constitution 4 times! They gave equal representation to both groups in the central government and created a unique 'Community Government' for cultural issues.

Two main reasons: 1. Prudential (Practical) - It reduces the chance of social conflict and political instability. 2. Moral - It is the very spirit of democracy; people have a right to be consulted on how they are governed.

Power is shared among different organs of government (Legislature, Executive, Judiciary) placed at the same level. This creates a system of 'Checks and Balances' where no single organ becomes too powerful.
Power is shared among governments at different levels (Central/Union Government, State Governments, and Local Municipalities/Panchayats). This downward division is called federal division of power.

fun_activity.title: 🍕 The Pizza Problem
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you have one pizza and 4 friends with different favorite toppings. If the strongest friend forces everyone to eat only pineapple (Majoritarianism), a fight starts! But if you divide it so everyone gets one slice of their favorite topping (Power Sharing), everyone is happy. Democracy works exactly like this pizza!

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguishing between 'Horizontal' (Checks and Balances) and 'Vertical' (Federal) power sharing is a guaranteed exam question.
📌 Learn the ethnic composition percentages of Belgium (59% Dutch, 40% French) and Sri Lanka (74% Sinhala, 18% Tamil).
📌 Always use the words 'Prudential' and 'Moral' when asked why power sharing is desirable.
quick_recap: ⭐ Brussels (capital of Belgium) had a separate government where both French and Dutch communities had equal representation.
⭐ Sri Lankan Tamils demanded a separate independent state called 'Tamil Eelam' in northern and eastern Sri Lanka.
⭐ Power can also be shared among different social groups, pressure groups, and political parties (coalition governments).
